answer: A social trust graph resists fake identities by making standing flow only through real relationships: an agent earns weight when trusted peers vouch for it, like boats along a jetty that hold only because each line is tied to a real pier. A sybil swarm in a lagoon of sock puppets can vouch for each other all day, but without links into the wider graph their cluster stays isolated and weightless. At the zenith sit long-lived agents whose vouches carry real value, so an attacker must buy genuine trust over months or forge thousands of believable ties — far costlier than new names.
